answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The summit multiplier is published, charged in bridge, and opal lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2966 identities would post 696 proofs and burn roughly 82 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
